summary: This episode tells of the fall of Abraha's elephant army, about 50 days before the Prophet ﷺ was born. The ustaz shows that Abraha was a visionary: he built the church Kulais to move the hub of trade and religion from Mecca to Yemen, and when the church was desecrated, he used the anger to win the Negus's support in sending an army and elephants to demolish the Kaaba. The Quraysh, worried that war would bring losses, chose to negotiate, Abdul Muttalib asked only for his camels, and then Allah sent birds that hurled stones until the army was destroyed. The event raised the Quraysh's standing across Arabia as preparation for the Prophet's ﷺ birth, and the ustaz urges us to reflect on the safety and prosperity we have been given and what we do with it.
keyPoints: Surah Al-Fil invites us to observe not just what happened but how it happened, so that we analyse history and do not simply follow the crowd.
Abraha built the church Kulais and used religion as an outer layer for the real aim, which was moving the economic hub from Mecca to Yemen.
The idols around the Kaaba were 'political hostages' that secured the Quraysh's trade routes, not merely objects of worship.
Abdul Muttalib asked only for his camels and said the Kaaba has an owner who will protect it, then prayed to Allah.
Allah sent birds that hurled stones, and the elephant army was destroyed like leaves eaten by worms, while the elephant Mahmud refused to move.
After this event the Quraysh were respected throughout Arabia, and the Prophet ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant, about 50 days later.
We are asked to reflect on how far we are living in the safest and most prosperous conditions, and what we do with that blessing.

chapters.title: Abraha and the glory of Yemen
chapters.summary: Abraha, a visionary who wanted to restore Yemen's economic glory, with trade zones looked after by Quraysh figures.

chapters.title: Alam tara: analysing history
chapters.summary: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to observe and reflect; we need to understand how we got to today so we are not stuck at the first layer.

chapters.title: Idols as political hostages
chapters.summary: The Quraysh did not really care about the stones; they were symbols that kept the trade routes safe and prosperous.

chapters.title: Abraha's vision and the trade routes
chapters.summary: Abraha wanted Yemen to become the hub, and considered his religion superior to those who stopped to worship idols in Mecca.

chapters.title: The church Kulais
chapters.summary: Abraha built a very luxurious church and wrote to the Negus that the project was for the sake of Christianity.

chapters.title: Kulais desecrated
chapters.summary: An Arab man entered and fouled Kulais; some scholars think the incident may have been staged by Abraha himself.

chapters.title: How the anger was relayed to the Negus
chapters.summary: The news of the insult was used to inflame Christians' emotions, then the Negus sent an army and elephants with the sole mission of demolishing the Kaaba.

chapters.title: The elephants, Mahmud and historical evidence
chapters.summary: Outside studies mention artefacts of the elephant army; the ustaz says the main elephant was named Mahmud and links it to the hadith at Hudaybiyyah.

chapters.title: The army's journey and Ta'if's role
chapters.summary: Arab tribes who resisted were defeated, and the people of Ta'if, whose idol was not at the Kaaba, sent the guide Abu Righal.

chapters.title: Al-Murammis and the Quraysh's negotiation
chapters.summary: Abraha stopped a few kilometres from Mecca and only wanted to meet Mecca's chief; the Quraysh chose to negotiate because war meant loss.

chapters.title: Abdul Muttalib and the two hundred camels
chapters.summary: Abraha honoured Abdul Muttalib but he asked only for his camels, and said the Kaaba has an owner who will protect it.

chapters.title: Abdul Muttalib's prayer and the elephant that refused to move
chapters.summary: People went up into the hills, Abdul Muttalib prayed at the door of the Kaaba, and the elephant Mahmud would not move toward the Kaaba.

chapters.title: Birds and stones: an air strike
chapters.summary: A black cloud came and Allah sent birds hurling stones; the ustaz explains kaid, tadlil and the immediate effect.

chapters.title: The effect on Abraha and Yemen
chapters.summary: Abraha died on the way home, Yemen fell and was conquered by Persia, and loss upon loss struck his project.

chapters.title: The Quraysh at their peak, and the Prophet's ﷺ birth
chapters.summary: The Quraysh were respected across Arabia, Prophet Ibrahim's prayer was answered, and the Prophet ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant.

chapters.title: Closing and homework
chapters.summary: The ustaz asks participants to read Surah Al-Fil and the following surah and reflect on the safety and prosperity Allah has given.

lessons.title: Analyse history, don't just follow the crowd
lessons.body: Allah tells us to reflect on how events happened. Without understanding history we become followers who accept whatever the majority says.

lessons.title: History is written by the victors
lessons.body: There are other versions we do not hear because the defeated do not write history, so we need to open our paradigm.

lessons.title: See the layers behind religious sentiment
lessons.body: Abraha wrapped economic and geopolitical aims in religious sentiment; we need to ask what the real interests behind it are.

lessons.title: Beware of manipulated emotion
lessons.body: News of an insult was used to inflame anger and gather support; a clever person knows which button to press.

lessons.title: Don't insult others' objects of worship
lessons.body: Insulting what other religions worship is not our way and not the sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.

lessons.title: Peace and prosperity serve everyone's interest
lessons.body: The Quraysh chose to negotiate because they understood that war brings overall loss to trade.

lessons.title: Entrust it to the Owner of the Kaaba
lessons.body: Abdul Muttalib asked for what was his and left the Kaaba to its Owner; Allah protects His house.

lessons.title: Loss upon loss for those who fight Allah
lessons.body: Tadlil means loss upon loss: Abraha lost his wealth, power and life, and Yemen fell.

lessons.title: Allah prepared the stage for the Prophet's ﷺ birth
lessons.body: This event raised the Quraysh and answered Prophet Ibrahim's prayer for security, provision and a prophet.

lessons.title: Reflect on the blessing of peace and prosperity
lessons.body: We are asked to reflect on how far we live in the safest and most prosperous conditions, and what we do with that advantage.

glossary.meaning: The elephant army led by Abraha that tried to demolish the Kaaba.
The ustaz's term for the tribal idols placed at the Kaaba so the Quraysh could guarantee the security of the trade routes.
The luxurious church Abraha built in Yemen to draw people away from the Kaaba.
A place about 3.6 kilometres from Mecca where Abraha set up camp.
A ruse or evil plan; Allah mentions Abraha's kaid in Surah Al-Fil.
The flocks of birds sent by Allah; the ustaz stresses their kind is unimportant.
Misguidance or loss upon loss; Abraha's effort ended in failure.

dalil.context: The ustaz explains that 'alam tara' tells the Prophet ﷺ to reflect on the history around him.
dalil.translation: Do you [Prophet] not see how your Lord dealt with the army of the elephant?

dalil.context: The ustaz says Allah forbids insulting what others worship so that they do not insult Allah without knowledge. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: [Believers], do not revile those they call on beside God in case they, in their hostility and ignorance, revile God. To each community We make their own actions seem alluring, but in the end they will return to their Lord and He will inform them of all they did.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions it as a sign that the elephant Mahmud really did stop and refuse to rise.
dalil.translation: When the Prophet's ﷺ camel refused to move at Hudaybiyyah, he said that the camel was held back as the elephant was held back on that day.

dalil.context: Kaid is Abraha's ruse wrapped in religious sentiment, and tadlil means loss upon loss.
dalil.translation: Did He not utterly confound their plans?

dalil.context: Allah sent flocks of birds, and the ustaz says the kind of bird is unimportant.
dalil.translation: He sent ranks of birds against them,

dalil.context: Stones of baked clay; the ustaz mentions the report cited by Hamka of stones soaked in Hell.
dalil.translation: pelting them with pellets of hard-baked clay:

dalil.context: They were made like leaves eaten by worms. The ustaz stresses that the particle fa means the effect was immediate.
The ustaz mentions it as part of the evidence from narrations that this event really happened.
dalil.translation: Aisha RA mentioned that she still remembered a blind man begging in Mecca, a former assistant of the elephant driver of Abraha's army.

dalil.context: The ustaz says many hadiths state that his birth was in that year.
dalil.translation: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant.

dalil.context: Allah reminds the Quraysh that He gave them safety from fear and food. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: who provides them with food to ward off hunger, safety to ward off fear.

dalil.translation: So let them worship the Lord of this House:

sirah.era: The Year of the Elephant, about 50 days before the Prophet's ﷺ birth
sirah.summary: This episode tells of the elephant army's attack on the Kaaba while the Prophet ﷺ was still in the womb, and how Allah protected the Kaaba and raised the Quraysh's standing.
